Package frc.robot.subsystems.shooter

Class ShooterIOHardware

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.subsystems.shooter.ShooterIOHardware
All Implemented Interfaces:
ShooterIO
public class ShooterIOHardware extends Object implements ShooterIO
Hardware implementation of ShooterIO that controls real TalonFX motors via CTRE Phoenix 6 CAN.

Shooter motors: two TalonFX motors, shooter 2 configured as a follower of shooter 1 so only shooter 1 receives control requests. Hood motor: one TalonFX with a CANcoder for absolute position feedback.

All status signals are registered with StatusSignalUtil in the constructor for bulk refresh at the start of each loop. This avoids the latency of individual blocking reads and is required by the CTRE Phoenix 6 best-practices for high-frequency loops.

      public void updateInputs(ShooterIO.ShooterIOInputs inputs)
      Description copied from interface: ShooterIO
      Reads all hardware sensor values into inputs. Must be called once per loop cycle before any other method so that callers see fresh data. All fields in ShooterIO.ShooterIOInputs are updated in place; the caller owns the inputs object across loops.

    • setVelocity

      public void setVelocity(edu.wpi.first.units.measure.AngularVelocity velocity, boolean useRecovery)
      Commands the shooter flywheel to spin at velocity.

      Two closed-loop modes are available, selected by useRecovery:

      • Normal mode (useRecovery = false): uses VelocityTorqueCurrentFOC â€” torque-based FOC control. Provides excellent speed stability and recovers quickly after a note passes through. This is the default for all match shooting.
      • Recovery mode (useRecovery = true): uses VelocityDutyCycle â€” voltage-based control. Less accurate but draws less current during brown-out conditions or when the battery is depleted. Use if the robot is tripping breakers or experiencing voltage sag.
      Passing zero velocity coasts the motor instead of actively braking.

      Optimization: the control request is only sent over CAN when the velocity or recovery mode changes. CAN bus traffic is reduced because this method is called every 20 ms loop cycle, but the setpoint typically changes much less frequently.

      Specified by:
      setVelocity in interface ShooterIO
      Parameters:
      velocity - Target flywheel speed.
      useRecovery - true to switch to the lower-current recovery control mode.
